_about: Reviewed corrections applied by the app on top of Cliopatria (state borders) and historical-basemaps (peoples layer). Each entry cites the specialist log in content/factcheck/ that found it. Operations on a Cliopatria realm (matched by its row name): clip [from,to] hides it outside those years; hide [[from,to],...] hides it inside them; relabel [{from,to,name,key,addTo?}] renames it in those years (key = colour/selection group; addTo = realms whose area timelines absorb the moved area); note = text shown on the realm; scholarly = peak-area estimate shown beside the map's. Base-layer operations by snapshot year: hide [names] turns a polygon into unrecorded land; rename {old: new}.

Ptolemaic Kingdom.note: Polygons dated 331–324 BCE, before Ptolemy took Egypt, are Alexander's conquests mislabelled in the data; they are shown as the Macedonian Empire. The Ptolemaic kingdom proper dates from 305 BCE.

Almohad Caliphate.note: The 1260–1343 polygon is the Marinid sultanate (the Almohads fell in 1269) and is shown under that name.

Mamluk Sultanate.note: The 1241–49 polygon duplicated Ayyubid Egypt and is hidden; the Mamluk sultanate begins in 1250.

Golden Horde.note: The Golden Horde ended in 1502; later polygons under its name are shown as its successor khanates. Cliopatria also starts it only in 1294 (it existed from the 1240s as part of the Mongol Empire).

Inca Empire.note: The Inca Empire fell to Spain in 1532–33. The large 1534–39 polygon is hidden; the remnant is shown as the Neo-Inca State of Vilcabamba (to 1572). The map also under-draws the empire before 1497.

Khmer Empire.note: The Angkorian empire ended c. 1431; later polygons are shown as the post-Angkor Kingdom of Cambodia.

Ngô Dynasty.note: The Ngô ruled 939–965 only; from 966 this polygon is Đại Việt under the Đinh, Early Lê, Lý, Trần and Hồ dynasties.

Sultanate of Malacca.note: Malacca fell to Portugal in 1511; later polygons under its name are its successor, Johor.

Natalia Republic.note: The Boer Natalia Republic was annexed by Britain in 1843; afterwards this polygon is the British Colony of Natal.

People's Republic of Zanzibar.note: In the 1800s this was the Sultanate of Zanzibar; the 'People's Republic' name dates from 1964.

Yuan Dynasty.note: Yuan rule in China ended in 1368; the remnant on the steppe is the Northern Yuan. Cliopatria starts the Yuan in 1294 (proclaimed 1271), and draws it larger than scholarly estimates.

Han Dynasty.note: The Han fell in 220 CE; later polygons are hidden. The map draws its peak smaller than scholarly estimates.

Sui Dynasty.note: The Sui fell in 618; later polygons are hidden.

Tibetan Empire.note: The Tibetan Empire collapsed in 842; later polygons are hidden.

Goguryeo.note: Goguryeo fell to Silla and Tang in 668; later polygons are hidden.

Shang Dynasty.note: The Shang fell to the Zhou c. 1046 BCE; later polygons are hidden. The map shows only the Shang core, far smaller than its sphere of influence.

Hunnic Empire.note: The Hunnic Empire broke up after Attila's death and was gone by 469; later polygons are hidden. Scholarly estimates of its peak are about twice the map's.

Parthian Empire.note: The Parthian Empire fell to the Sasanians in 224 CE; later polygons are hidden.

Saadi Sultanate.note: The Saadi dynasty ended in 1659; later polygons are hidden (the Alaouites took Morocco in the 1660s).

Sur Empire.note: The Sur Empire fell to the Mughals in 1556–57; later polygons are hidden.

Gran Colombia.note: Gran Colombia dissolved in 1830–31; later polygons are hidden.

Greek City-States.note: Greece came under Roman control in 146 BCE; later polygons are hidden.

Sasanian Empire.note: Cliopatria ends the Sasanian Empire in 643; it fell with Yazdegerd III's death in 651.

Tang Dynasty.note: Cliopatria starts the Tang in 623 (founded 618) and draws it larger than scholarly estimates.

Ming Dynasty.note: Cliopatria starts the Ming in 1375; it was proclaimed in 1368.

Qing Dynasty.note: Cliopatria starts the Qing in 1645; it was proclaimed in 1636 (1619–44 is drawn as the Later Jin). The map's peak is below scholarly estimates.

Mongol Empire.note: The map's peak exceeds scholarly estimates of the empire's extent.

Ilkhanate.note: Cliopatria starts the Ilkhanate in 1294; it was founded in 1256 (earlier it is drawn inside the Mongol Empire).

Chagatai Khanate.note: Cliopatria starts the Chagatai Khanate in 1294; it existed from the 1220s (earlier it is drawn inside the Mongol Empire).

Xiongnu.note: Scholarly estimates of the Xiongnu peak are much larger than the map's.

Seleucid Empire.note: The map's peak is below scholarly estimates.

Abbasid Caliphate.note: The map's peak is below scholarly estimates.

Ottoman Empire.note: The map's peak (1595) is below the scholarly estimate for 1683.

Kievan Rus'.note: The map's extent is below scholarly estimates.

Maratha Empire.note: The map has no Maratha polygon for 1691–1717 and draws its 18th-century sphere far smaller than Schwartzberg (pl. VII.A) and Turchin.

(Delhi Sultanate).note: Scholars differ on the peak: Taagepera and Turchin put it in 1312 under Alauddin Khalji; Schwartzberg (pl. V) and this map show the widest extent under Muhammad bin Tughluq in the 1330s.

Khalji Dynasty.note: Taagepera and Turchin estimate c. 3.2M km² for 1312, far more than drawn here; Schwartzberg (pl. V) shows the Khalji sphere reaching the far south only through tributary raids.

British Raj.note: Cliopatria keeps Burma inside the Raj after its separation in 1937 (except 1943–44), and has no Raj polygon before 1859 (Crown rule began 1858).

Vijayanagara Empire.note: Cliopatria ends Vijayanagara in 1571; its Aravidu kings ruled on until 1646.

Chola Empire.note: Cliopatria ends the Chola in 1259 (dynasty ended 1279). No scholarly peak-area estimate exists; the map's c. 0.5M km² is smaller than older estimates.

People's Republic of Bangladesh.note: Cliopatria starts Bangladesh in 1973; it became independent in 1971.

Republic of China.note: After 1950 the map shows c. 81,000 km², about twice the area of Taiwan and its islands (c. 36,000 km²).

Kingdom of Kongo.note: Cliopatria draws Kongo only for 1440–1669; the kingdom lasted from c. 1390 to 1914.

Empire of Kanem.note: Drawn far too small and starting too late; Kanem is attested from 872.

Chámpa.note: Cliopatria ends Champa in 1652; it survived as a Vietnamese vassal until 1832.

Srivijaya.note: Srivijaya's end date is debated (11th–14th century).

Canada.note: Cliopatria starts Canada in 1932; Confederation was in 1867 (earlier Canada is drawn within the British Empire).

South Africa.note: Cliopatria starts South Africa in 1932; the Union of South Africa was formed in 1910.

Commonwealth of Australia.note: Cliopatria starts Australia in 1905; federation was in 1901.

New Zealand.note: Cliopatria starts New Zealand in 1948; it was a British colony from 1840 and a dominion from 1907.

Kingdom of Hungary.note: Cliopatria ends the Kingdom of Hungary in 1546; under the Habsburgs it continued until 1918.

Xianbei.note: Tanshihuai unified the Xianbei c. 156 and his confederation reached from the Wusun in the west to the Buyeo in the east, but it splintered after his death in 181; Kebineng's later revival (c. 207–235) was centred near the Great Wall. The data's polygon also runs north into Dingling lands south of Lake Baikal, a people Tanshihuai pushed back rather than ruled. For 182–223 the Xianbei are shown as tribes rather than a state.

scholarly.source: List of largest empires (Wikipedia), citing an Oxford reference
